The Reds | founded = {{Start date and age|1903|4|14|df=yes}} | ground = [[Pittodrie Stadium]] | capacity = 19,274{{cite web|url=https://x.com/AFCspareTickets/status/1959226531563102289|title=AFCSpareTickets|access-date=24 August 2025}} | chairman = [[Dave Cormack]] | manager = [[Stephen Robinson (footballer)|Stephen Robinson]] | league = {{Scottish football updater|Aberdeen}} | season = {{Scottish football updater|Aberdeen2}} | position = {{Scottish football updater|Aberdeen3}} | website = {{URL|https://www.afc.co.uk/|afc.co.uk}} | pattern_la1 = _aberdeen2526h | pattern_b1 = _aberdeen2526h | pattern_ra1 = _aberdeen2526h | pattern_sh1 = _aberdeen2526h | pattern_so1 = _adidasonredl | leftarm1 = fF0000 | body1 = fF0000 | rightarm1 = fF0000 | shorts1 = fF0000 | socks1 = 880000 | pattern_la2 = _aberdeen2627a | pattern_b2 = _aberdeen2627a | pattern_ra2 = _aberdeen2627a | pattern_sh2 = _aberdeen2627a | pattern_so2 = _aberdeen2627al | leftarm2 = 000029 | body2 = 000029 | rightarm2 = 000029 | shorts2 = 000029 | socks2 = 000029 | pattern_la3 = | pattern_b3 = | pattern_ra3 = | pattern_sh3 = | pattern_so3 = | leftarm3 = | body3 = | rightarm3 = | shorts3 = | socks3 = }} '''Aberdeen Football Club''' is a Scottish professional [[Association football|football]] club based in [[Aberdeen]], Scotland. They compete in the {{Scottish football updater|Aberdeen}} and have [[List of unrelegated association football clubs|never been relegated]] from the top division of the [[Scottish football league system]] since they were elected to the top flight in 1905.{{cite web |last=Nardelli |first=Alberto |title=Which European football clubs have never been relegated? |url=https://www.theguardian.com/news/datablog/2015/jun/02/which-european-football-clubs-have-never-been-relegated |quote=Only two clubs have always played in Scotland's top division: Celtic (since 1890) and Aberdeen (since 1905). |access-date=7 April 2024 |website=[[The Guardian]] |date=2 June 2015 |archive-date=7 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240407100141/https://www.theguardian.com/news/datablog/2015/jun/02/which-european-football-clubs-have-never-been-relegated |url-status=live}} Aberdeen have won four [[list of Scottish football champions|Scottish league titles]], eight [[Scottish Cup]]s and six [[Scottish League Cup]]s. They are also the only Scottish team to have won two European trophies, having won the [[UEFA Cup Winners' Cup|European Cup Winners' Cup]] and the [[UEFA Super Cup|European Super Cup]] in 1983. Formed in 1903 as a result of the amalgamation of three clubs from Aberdeen, they rarely challenged for honours until the post-war decade, when they won each of the major Scottish trophies under manager [[Dave Halliday]]. This level of success was surpassed in the 1980s, when, under the management of [[Alex Ferguson]], they won three league titles, four Scottish Cups and a Scottish League Cup, alongside the two European trophies. Aberdeen were the last club outside the [[Old Firm]] to win a league title, in [[1984–85 in Scottish football|1984–85]], and also the last Scottish team to win a European trophy. They have enjoyed less success since this golden era, though in the 2010s, the club ended a 19-year wait for a major trophy by winning the [[2013–14 Scottish League Cup]]; this was followed by four consecutive seasons of finishing second behind [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] in the league. More triumph came in 2025 as they won the [[2024–25 Scottish Cup|Scottish Cup]] for the first time in 35 years. Aberdeen have played at [[Pittodrie Stadium]] since their inception. The ground has a capacity of 19,274,{{cite web|url=https://x.com/AFCspareTickets/status/1959226531563102289|title=AFCSpareTickets|access-date=24 August 2025}} and was the first [[All-seater stadium|all-seated]] and all-covered stadium in the United Kingdom. Pittodrie was also the first football stadium to feature a [[technical area|dug-out]], an invention of player and coach [[Donald Colman]]. The club's colours have been primarily red and white since 1939; before this, they played in black and gold vertical stripes. In modern times, Aberdeen have almost exclusively played with all-red strips with white detailing.{{cite web|url=http://historicalkits.co.uk/Scottish_Football_League/Aberdeen/Aberdeen.htm|title=Aberdeen|publisher=Historical Football Kits|access-date=23 November 2017|archive-date=1 December 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201035419/http://historicalkits.co.uk/Scottish_Football_League/Aberdeen/Aberdeen.htm|url-status=live}} Aberdeen attract support from the city and surrounding areas, as they have no geographically close rivals. Lacking a local competitor, Aberdeen have instead developed rivalries with more distant opponents such as [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] (collectively known as the "[[New Firm (Scotland)|New Firm]]" in the 1980s) and [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]]."}}
